item.title: Hip & Pelvis — Traction / Distraction
clinicalUse: Use when assessment identifies a relevant impairment in Hip & Pelvis and the parent technique fits the patient's presentation.
Primary treatment target: hip mobility, pelvic/SI-region symptoms, gait and functional loading.
Retain the technique only if it produces a meaningful within-session improvement.
patientPosition: Supine, prone or side-lying with the pelvis well supported.
Use a comfortable hip position and avoid forcing painful end range.
therapistPosition: Stand close to the pelvis/hip and use a belt when appropriate and trained.
stabilization: Stabilize pelvis when targeting the hip; stabilize the trunk/leg according to the pelvic technique.
contact: Use broad contact over proximal femur, pelvis or target soft tissue; avoid excessive pressure over groin neurovascular structures.
Support the segment close to the joint/region and create a comfortable distraction rather than a sudden pull.
forceDirection: Apply smooth longitudinal or joint-plane distraction and begin with very low force.
Continue only if symptoms centralize, pain decreases or movement becomes easier.
dosage: Trial 10–30 second holds repeated 3–5 times, individualized to response.
steps: 1. Record the exact comparable sign for Hip & Pelvis: hip mobility, pelvic/SI-region symptoms, gait and functional loading.
2. Screen regional red flags, contraindications and technique-specific precautions before touching the patient.
3. Position and stabilize the patient so the target is comfortable and the manual input can be localized.
4. Apply a low-force trial using the parent technique principles and the region-specific contact described above.
5. Monitor pain quality, symptom distribution, guarding and patient confidence throughout.
6. Re-test the original comparable sign immediately after the trial.
7. Keep the technique only when the response is useful, then transfer the gain into active movement, loading or self-management.
mistakes: Applying the technique because it is familiar rather than because the examination supports it.
Using more force when the response is unclear or worsening.
Failing to re-test the exact movement or function that justified the treatment.
safety: Screen fracture, severe OA irritability, postoperative restrictions, acute inflammatory pathology and red-flag pelvic symptoms.
Stop or modify if symptoms peripheralize, neurological status worsens, the response is disproportionate or the patient asks to stop.
item.visualCue: Hip & Pelvis assessment → correct regional setup → Traction / Distraction → immediate comparable-sign re-test.

subTechniques.name: Hip Long-Axis Distraction
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Reduce compression sensitivity and prepare mobility
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine, prone or side-lying with pelvis stabilized.
subTechniques.contact: Region-specific contact over Hip joint using the parent technique principles.
subTechniques.dosage: Use a conservative response-guided trial and reassess before repeating.
